title: Mimicry of chaos and $k$-design in higher order OTOCs of Luttinger liquids
authors: Balázs Dóra, Catalin Pascu Moca, Roderich Moessner
abstract: Out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) provide a fundamental metric for quantum chaos, but capturing the fine structure of information scrambling requires exploring their higher-order generalizations. Here, we systematically investigate the sequence of higher-order OTOCs in a Luttinger liquid and its lattice realization, the XXZ Heisenberg chain. Using bosonization and numerics, we extract the full temporal dynamics of the first three OTOCs, revealing that they rapidly erase memory of the initial state, and quickly saturate to their steady state values. Strikingly, we show that calculating the late time saturation values for the entire sequence of higher-order OTOCs maps exactly onto determining the partition function of a non-Hermitian Harper model. Through this mapping, we demonstrate that for moderately strong interactions, the steady-state OTOCs become parametrically small up to the seventh order, mimicking higher $k$-design. Our results reveal that Luttinger liquids exhibit an unexpectedly profound degree of apparent scrambling when viewed through the lens of higher-order OTOCs.
summary: The paper analyzes higher-order Out-of-Time-Order Correlators in Luttinger liquids to probe information scrambling. By mapping the late-time saturation of these correlators onto the partition function of a non-Hermitian Harper model, the authors demonstrate that LLs exhibit complex, apparent chaotic behavior even when viewed through high-order diagnostics.
main_problem: The study investigates higher-order generalizations of Out-of-Time-Order Correlators (OTOCs) to provide a detailed metric for quantum chaos and information scrambling in interacting quantum systems.
main_result: Higher-order OTOCs saturate to steady-state values that map exactly onto the partition function of a non-Hermitian Harper model, revealing an unexpectedly profound degree of apparent scrambling in Luttinger liquids.
method: The authors employ bosonization techniques and detailed numerical calculations to extract the time evolution of higher-order correlators up to the seventh order.
model_or_system: The primary systems studied are Luttinger liquids (LL) and their lattice realization, the spin-1/2 XXZ Heisenberg chain. The analysis uses low-energy bosonic descriptions derived from these models.
key_observables: Higher-order OTOCs, denoted $C(2k)(t)$, which measure information scrambling and are compared to indicators of quantum chaos like higher-$k$-design formation.
important_parameters: The Luttinger liquid parameter ($K$) controls the interaction strength; the analysis distinguishes between non-interacting ($K=1$) and interacting regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the validity of the LL description for low-energy physics, and approximations are made regarding power law decaying terms in the late time limit.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the fast saturation of $C(6)$, $C(4)$, and $C(2)$ to steady states. For stronger interactions ($\Delta=0.6$), these steady-state values approach zero, mimicking high scrambling with unitary 2-, 4-, and 6-design structures.
paper_structure: The paper systematically introduces OTOCs, develops the formalism for higher-order correlators using bosonization, calculates their time evolution in LL/XXZ chains, establishes the mapping to the Harper model partition function, and interprets the results regarding $k$-design formation.
why_interesting: This work connects advanced concepts of quantum chaos (OTOCs) with specific condensed matter models (LL), providing a powerful diagnostic tool for characterizing scrambling dynamics beyond standard quadratic measures.
